1. (Currently amended) A method for controlling a flow of air, the method comprising: establishing a level of vacuum in a booster device by generating the flow of air from the booster device using a pump; determining whether the level of vacuum in the booster device has reached a predetermined value; __monitoring a pressure differential across the pump;__ and terminating the flow of air from the booster device when the level of vacuum in the booster device has reached the predetermined value __while maintaining the pump in an operational state to preserve the pressure differential across the pump__.

2. (Currently amended) The method of claim 1, wherein said terminating the flow of air is accomplished via a directional control valve, such that __the__ pressure differential across the pump is __maintained while the pump remains operational__.

3. (Currently amended) The method of claim 2, wherein said terminating the flow of air includes changing the direction of the flow of air and closing a flow path between the pump and the booster device __while maintaining the pump in continuous operation__.

4. (Currently amended) The method of claim 3, wherein said changing the direction of the flow of air includes opening a flow path between a negative pressure chamber of the pump and a positive pressure chamber of the pump __while the pump continues to operate__.

5. (Currently amended) The method of claim 3, wherein said changing the direction of the flow of air includes opening a path for a flow of air between the pump and the atmosphere __while maintaining pump operation__.

6. (Currently amended) The method of claim 5, further comprising filtering the flow of air between the atmosphere and the pump via __a dedicated__ filter __positioned in the flow path__.

7. (Previously presented) The method of claim 1, wherein the booster device is a vacuum servo booster for an automobile braking system.

8. (Currently amended) A system for controlling a flow of air, the system comprising: a booster device configured to provide a vacuum assist when a level of vacuum has been established in the device; a pump configured to establish the level of vacuum in the booster device by generating the flow of air from the booster device; __a pressure monitoring device configured to monitor a pressure differential across the pump;__ and a directional control valve adapted to terminate the flow of air from the booster device when the level of vacuum in the booster device has reached a predetermined value, such that __the__ pressure differential across the pump is __maintained while the pump remains operational__.

9. (Currently amended) The system of claim 8, wherein the directional control valve is further adapted to change the direction of the flow of air and close a flow path between the pump and the booster device __while maintaining the pump in continuous operation__.

10. (Currently amended) The system of claim 9, wherein to change the direction of the flow of air the directional control valve opens a flow path between a negative pressure chamber of the pump and a positive pressure chamber of the pump __while the pump continues to operate__.

11. (Currently amended) The system of claim 9, wherein to change the direction of the flow of air the directional control valve opens a flow path between the pump and the atmosphere __while maintaining pump operation__.

12. (Currently amended) The system of claim 11, further comprising __a dedicated__ filter adapted for filtering a flow of air between the atmosphere and the pump __positioned in the flow path__.

13. (Previously presented) The system of claim 8, wherein the booster device is a vacuum servo booster for an automobile braking system.

14. (Currently amended) A motor vehicle comprising: an internal combustion engine; a booster device configured to provide a vacuum assist when a level of vacuum has been established in the device; and a system for controlling a flow of air from the booster device, the system including: a pump configured to establish the level of vacuum in the booster device by generating the flow of air from the booster device; __a pressure monitoring device configured to monitor a pressure differential across the pump;__ and a directional control valve adapted to terminate the flow of air from the booster device when the level of vacuum in the booster device has reached a predetermined value, such that __the__ pressure differential across the pump __is maintained while the pump remains operational__ and a parasitic load on the engine __is controlled__.

15. (Currently amended) The vehicle of claim 14, wherein the directional control valve is further adapted to change the direction of the flow of air and close a flow path between the pump and the booster device __while maintaining the pump in continuous operation__.

16. (Currently amended) The vehicle of claim 15, wherein to change the direction of the flow of air the directional control valve opens a flow path between a negative pressure chamber of the pump and a positive pressure chamber of the pump __while the pump continues to operate__.

17. (Currently amended) The vehicle of claim 15, wherein to change the direction of the flow of air the directional control valve opens a flow path between the pump and the atmosphere __while maintaining pump operation__.

18. (Currently amended) The vehicle of claim 17, further comprising __a dedicated__ filter adapted for filtering the flow of air between the atmosphere and the pump __positioned in the flow path__.

19. (Previously presented) The vehicle of claim 14, further comprising a braking system, wherein the booster device is a vacuum servo booster for the braking system.

20. (Previously presented) The vehicle of claim 14, wherein the engine is a compression-ignition type.
